definition: A secure version of HTTP that encrypts data between your browser and websites, protecting information from being intercepted by third parties during transmission.
metaDescription: Learn about HTTPS - the secure protocol that encrypts your web browsing data. Understand why the padlock icon matters for your online privacy and security.
simpleExplanation: HTTPS is like sending a letter in a locked box instead of a postcard. When you visit a website with HTTPS, all the information you send and receive is scrambled so only you and the website can read it.
whyItMatters: HTTPS prevents hackers from stealing your passwords, credit card numbers, and personal information when you browse the web. It also helps verify that you're actually connecting to the real website, not a fake one.
technicalDetail: HTTPS uses Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption to create a secure tunnel between client and server. It operates on port 443 and requires SSL/TLS certificates to establish encrypted connections, ensuring data integrity, confidentiality, and authentication.

examples.explanation: When you log into your bank account, HTTPS encrypts your username and password so hackers on public WiFi can't steal your credentials.
E-commerce sites use HTTPS during checkout to protect your credit card information and billing address from being intercepted.
HTTPS on social platforms prevents others from seeing which profiles you visit or what messages you send, even on shared networks.
